subject: Direction update: QBR prep, scope trade-offs & blocker clearance
messages:
From: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-10T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Direction update: QBR prep, scope trade-offs & blocker clearance

Team —

Quick leadership update as we start QBR prep: overall feedback from last week’s exec review is that we need clearer trade-offs across three focus OKRs (Serving Runtime perf, Dedicated capacity roadmap, and Console observability). The ask from execs is: reduce scope where possible to hit a clean set of deliverables for the QBR demo and have clear dependency owners for everything else.

Key notes:
- Proposed scope trims: shift non-critical Dashboard visualizations to post-QBR (nice-to-have).
- Keep the Serving Runtime P0 perf improvements (KV cache + batching) intact — these are customer-visible.
- For Dedicated roadmap, drop the advanced autoscaling heuristics from Q4 deliverables and mark as stretch.

Immediate asks from this thread: please reply with two things by EOD Monday (2026-10-12):
1) Your committed scope for the next 30 days (what you will deliver for QBR)
2) Top 3 blockers or cross-team dependencies and an owner for each

I attached a short QBR prep brief and a dependency tracker to help format responses. I’ll consolidate and send the exec-facing one-pager Wednesday morning.

attachment: QBR-prep-brief-v1.pdf (pdf)
attachment: Dependency-Rollup-Tracker.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks —
Jasmine Liu
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-10T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Direction update: QBR prep, scope trade-offs & blocker clearance

Thanks, Jas — good distillation. My consolidated reply below. I copied the Dependency-Rollup sheet with inline owners.

Committed scope (next 30 days):
- Deliver: Exec-facing latency improvement slides + before/after perf numbers for 99th p99 for the Serving Runtime KV cache change.
- Demo-ready: streaming latency example with 2k token sequences (basic dashboard widget only).

Top 3 blockers + owners:
1) GPU infra quota for large perf runs — owner: vivek_kulkarni (infra request in flight; needs approval for 6x spot nodes)
2) End-to-end tracing hook in Console to show request path in demo — owner: laura_bennett (needs 2 engineering days and a small policy change)
3) Test corpus coverage gap for long-tail prompts — owner: naomi_feldman (we can cut to a representative subset to save infra)

Notes: I can compress the perf runs by running targeted long tails if infra is provisioned. If infra approval slips beyond Thurs, we should pivot the demo to a synthetic workload and call it out.

attachment: Dependency-Rollup-Tracker.xlsx (updated tab: ServingRuntime)

-naomi
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-11T09:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Direction update: QBR prep, scope trade-offs & blocker clearance

On infra quota: I pushed the 6x spot node request through and flagged it for accelerated procurement (ticket INFRA-2339). ETA from cloud team if approved today: 48 hours for provisioning and initial smoke runs. If procurement stalls, we can borrow capacity from the Dedicated sandbox (with cost backcharge to Product).

Resource ask (decision point): do we want dedicated priority for the perf window (I recommend yes) — that will cost roughly $5k one-time for the reserved window. If leadership prefers to avoid cost, we will run targeted synthetic/localized runs instead (less convincing for execs).

Also: I can assign a small ops engineer (Karthik) to help with the KV cache rollout; he’ll need two dedicated half-days to instrument the runs. Owner: vivek_kulkarni (ops coordination).

If we commit to the Dedicated sandbox option, we should reflect the cost and rollback plan in the exec one-pager.

-vivek
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-11T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Direction update: QBR prep, scope trade-offs & blocker clearance

Acknowledged. For the Console tracing hook: I can re-prioritize the two eng days — ETA to deliver a demo-quality path is Tue (2026-10-13) EOD assuming the infra is available for an integrated smoke test.

Commitments succinct:
- Console: tracing hook + single dashboard widget for demo (owner: laura_bennett)
- Serving Runtime: prioritized KV cache perf + targeted long-tail test set (owner: naomi_feldman)
- Dedicated roadmap: shift advanced autoscaling to stretch, keep capacity/reservation story for QBR (owner: vivek_kulkarni)

I'll update the Dependency-Rollup tracker with these owners and put a confidence flag on each item.

-laura
From: Sarah Cole <sarah.cole@acme.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Corp Execs <execs@acme.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Direction update: QBR prep, scope trade-offs & blocker clearance

Thanks for the transparency — appreciate the trade-off call. From Acme’s side we strongly prefer the KV cache perf story in the demo over the extra Dashboard polish. The execs want to see measurable latency improvements on real-ish workloads.

A couple of asks from us:
- If you end up using the Dedicated sandbox for the perf window, please send a one-line note on cost impact so procurement can sign off on our side.
- If you pivot to a synthetic workload, please include a short justification slide about representativeness.

We’ll plan to be available for a dry-run on Oct 16; let us know preferred time slots.

Best,
Sarah Cole
VP Product, Acme Corp
